target_customer: Pharmaceutical partners that license or co-develop drug targets, and eventually patients via its own therapeutics
problem: Drug discovery struggles to identify which RNA and gene programs drive disease; Algen uses CRISPR gene modulation with single cell readouts and AI to find them.
business_model: Drug discovery platform with pharma partnerships (upfront, research funding and milestones) and internal pipeline
product_category: Biotech, CRISPR and AI drug discovery

founders.name: Chun-Hao Huang
prior_employers: UC Berkeley, postdoc fellow in the Jennifer Doudna lab
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Degrees not stated there.

founders.name: Christine Du
founders.background_notes: YC page describes the team as including a biotech commercialization expert; no details for her.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs CRISPR modulation at single cell resolution, wet lab pipelines and ML to find drug targets; research grade work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary perturbation datasets and Berkeley licensed IP create some barrier, but the approach is also pursued by academic and CRO groups.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it per sources found. A pharma partner, AstraZeneca, signed a multi target deal in October 2025.

market_need_then: Pharma spends heavily on target discovery and genome wide CRISPR screens were spreading as a discovery tool by the late 2010s, per industry reviews.

branding.domain_note: Uses algenbio.com, not the .com of the bare name.
branding.community_and_virality: No consumer community; press attention centers on the AstraZeneca deal and a TIME Best Inventions mention listed on the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: B2B science brand known mainly through partnership press; no brand-specific coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Algen is active and signed a multi target immunology partnership with AstraZeneca in October 2025 worth up to 555 million dollars in total payments per press reports, with an undisclosed upfront. Founder ties to the Doudna lab gave scientific credibility. Round details are poorly sourced, so funding strength cannot be fully judged.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights total 12.63M, VCBacked 5.4M, Reuters via The Star says about 11M previously raised; an aggregator mentions a roughly 9M seed in Feb 2022 led by Viking Global (single aggregator, not recorded as a round). Competitor search found only later or generic CRISPR screening vendors with no sources dated near 2020, so the list is empty. Company website fetch was rate limited, not fetched. Berkeley IPIRA page lists additional founders or inventors (Doudna, Spencer Knight, Nami Saghaei), unverified role.
